\title[Scott--Vogelius elements on polygonal walls]{Scott--Vogelius elements on polygonal approximations of curved walls: the zero-gradient lock, Nitsche's method and the penalty threshold}

\author*[1]{\fnm{Jaideep Sai} \sur{Padhi}}\email{jpadhi@purdue.edu}

%% Abstract rewritten 2026-09-29 for the companion-paper framing (150--250 words); it leads with the
%% material that is not in the AML letter \cite{CavalcantePadhiLetter}. No claim is added.
\abstract{Scott--Vogelius elements give pointwise divergence-free velocities, but when a curved no-slip wall is replaced by an inscribed polygon, strongly imposed no-slip can force a zero velocity gradient at polygon vertices, and the $H^1$ error can degrade to order $h^{1/2}$. Gjerde and Scott therefore imposed the wall condition by Nitsche's method, and Scott asked whether the error is $O(h_\Gamma^{3/2}+h_\Omega^k)$ and, if not, why not. A letter written jointly with C. de S. Cavalcante announces the core answer with proof sketches: the printed method leaks through the wall at the rate $(h/\mu)(p-\bar p)$ unless the wall pressure is constant, and a mean-free pressure traction restores Scott's rate. This companion paper contains what the letter does not. First, we determine when the zero-gradient lock occurs: under the Guzm\'an--Scott angle condition strongly imposed no-slip already has $H^1$ error $\asymp h_\Gamma^{3/2}+h^k$, and the lock comes from wall vertices lying in only two triangles, each costing $h_\Gamma|\partial_n u(z)|$. Second, we give the penalty theory: the penalty must scale with the ratio of bulk to boundary mesh size, as shown by exact certificates on shape families and a proof on every shape-regular mesh, while exact counterexamples show that necessity is not local. Third, we identify the $H^1$ constant of the leak as the energy of a Stokes leak flow. Finally, we give complete proofs of the letter's results, including the sharpness of $h_\Gamma^{3/2}$ for every $k\ge4$. Computations confirm the rates and constants.}

\keywords{Stokes equations, Scott--Vogelius elements, Nitsche's method, curved boundaries, divergence-free finite elements, penalty parameter}

\pacs[MSC Classification]{65N30 (primary), 65N12, 65N15, 76D07}
